stories.text: On 11 November 1927 a memorial designed by the City Engineer Thomas Wallis Gordon was unveiled on land beside the Trent given by Sir Jesse Boot. It remembers the men of Nottingham who died in both World Wars.

65160.sum: The City War Memorial, Nottingham, also known as the Nottingham Municipal War Memorial and the City of Nottingham War Memorial, is the main war memorial for the city of Nottingham in England. It comprises a memorial arch of Portland stone with three openings and wrought iron gates, and stone flanking arcades. It was unveiled in 1927 beside a new park overlooking the River Trent, and became a Grade II listed building in 1972.

stories.text: The Council House, designed by Thomas Cecil Howitt, opened in 1929 on the site of the old Exchange at the head of the Old Market Square.[^s1][^s1] The sculptor Joseph Else named the two stone lions on its steps Agamemnon and Menelaus.[^s1][^s1] Little John, the hour bell in its dome, weighs over 10 tonnes, and its strike can be heard 7 miles away.[^s1][^s1]

From 1283 the borough of Nottingham sent two members to Parliament. In the mid-18th century the great landowners, the Duke of Newcastle for the Whigs and Lord Middleton for the Tories, held sway, and the town usually returned one of each. In 1885 the old two-member seat was abolished, and the city was divided into three seats of one member each: Nottingham East, South and West.
The architect Thomas Cecil Howitt designed the Council House.[^s1][^s2]

74840.sum: The Nottingham Council House is the former city hall of Nottingham, England. The 200 feet high dome that rises above the city is the centrepiece of the skyline and presides over the Old Market Square, which is also referred to as the "City Centre". The building is Grade II* listed, and has retail units at street-level.
